question.problem:
A scientist measured $5$ particular features, ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{5},$ for each athlete among a group of athletes. The collected data was stored in the standardized observation matrix $X,$ where each row contains measurements for a particular athlete.
The singular values of $X$ are 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}=5,\,{\sigma }_{2}=2,\,{\sigma }_{3}=1,\,{\sigma }_{4}=0.5,\,{\sigma }_{5}=0.1.
$$

The scientist then converted the original observation matrix $X$ into a new matrix $Y$ using the equation $Y=X{V}_{2},$ where ${V}_{2}$ is the $5\times 2$ matrix consisting of the first two principal components of the data. What percentage of the original variance is preserved in the new transformed matrix $Y$ compared to the initial observation matrix $X?$
question.worked_solution:
Let $V$ be the matrix of principal components. Then, applying the change of variables

$$
Y=XV
$$

we can convert our observation matrix $X$ into a new matrix $Y$ of (linearly) transformed observations such that

- the covariance matrix of $Y$ is diagonal (meaning that the new features ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{5}$ are uncorrelated),

- the features ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{5}$ are arranged in order of decreasing variance, and

- the squares of the singular values ${\sigma }_{1}^{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2},…,{\sigma }_{5}^{2}$ represent the variances in the respective features ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{5}.$

Now, the total variance over all features is proportional to the sum of the squared singular values:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Total} & ∝{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{\sigma }_{i}^{2} \\  & =(5)^{2}+(2)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(0.5)^{2}+(0.1)^{2} \\  & =30.26\end{aligned}
$$

Since the scientist used only the first two principal components, the remaining variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Remaining} & ∝{\sum }_{i=1}^{2}{\sigma }_{i}^{2} \\  & =(5)^{2}+(2)^{2} \\  & =29.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our required percentage can be computed as

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{Remaining}}{\text{Total}} & =\frac{29}{30.26} \\  & ≈0.958 \\  & =95.8%.\end{aligned}
$$
